Infora · build layer · reference

The five-drawer data model

All 43 stored tables as built — drawn from packages/db/src/schema/drawer1–5 at migration 0030 (2026-07-26, branch slice-a2-producing-side-surfaces). Chips point at each table's foreign keys, tinted by the drawer they land in; badges mark the integrity rules the database itself enforces by trigger. The prose spec this reflects is docs/build/data-model.md.

The same 43 tables, re-classed by what each row is rather than which drawer stores it: agents & settings, information artifacts, the provenance chain, normative positions (time-indexed rights and duties), and institutional acts (irrevocable declarations that change the normative graph). Edges are the foreign keys; the one dashed edge is canReadDeliverable — the wall, a derived relation computed from the normative sub-graph, never stored. Node size is degree: the hub is the deliverable, not the project. Drag nodes; hover for detail; click a class to isolate it.

100%
scroll / pinch to zoom · drag space to pan · drag a node to move it

Reading it: the normative ring (ochre) sits between agents and artifacts — every path from a person to a document passes through a time-indexed grant, which is the ethical wall stated topologically. The acts (oxide) cluster against the artifacts they freeze; the provenance chain (violet) hangs off the working document and terminates in signals — the moat's inlet.

DRAWER 1Parties & access6 tables DRAWER 2Documents16 tables DRAWER 3Execution5 tables DRAWER 4Output & signal3 tables DRAWER 5Review & sharing13 tables

The grain of the system: parties gate everything → documents are worked in the sandbox, bound, frozen → review issues & accepts them into the library → agent runs (execution) propose output whose signals feed back — and drawer 5's grants decide who may see any of it.

DRAWER 1

Parties & access

drawer1-parties.ts

Who exists and what they may touch. The ethical wall (ADR-0018) is computed from these rows — organisations are isolated by default; a participant row is a person's live entitlement on one project.

organisations

A firm on the platform — the tenant grain of the ethical wall.

id · name

users

A person, belonging to exactly one organisation. Carries the org-admin role and the Entra seam for production identity.

organisation_id · org_role · external_identity · preferences

Skeleton email + password (scrypt) — dropped wholesale at the infra/security session (T-021).

user_id · password_hash

The owner organisation's project — the container for everything below.

owner_organisation_id · name

memberships

An organisation's seat on a project (owner / member), with the ADR-0035 acknowledgement mode and controller.

role · state · ack_mode · ack_controller_participant_id

participants

A user's live entitlement on one project; elevated is the super-user flag (T-174/176). Closing the interval revokes forward, never retroactively.

The deliverable record: coded reference, lifecycle state (planned → in_library / rejected / withdrawn), producing organisation, plan metadata.

DRAWER 3

Execution

drawer3-execution.ts

Work and the agent's audited doing (ADR-0028). Every run writes an immutable tree; the whole record is producing-organisation-private background data (the 2026-07-12 liability ruling, T-104).

work_items

A deliverable's work half, 1:1 with its container by type — status is event-driven, never hand-set (ADR-0032 addendum).

project_id · container_id · type · status
projectscontainersparticipants

conversations

A thread — Ask, a document's shared multiplayer thread (visibility rides the sandbox scope, ADR-0039), or Copilot-bound.

project_id · work_item_id · sandbox_document_id · surface
projectswork_itemssandbox_documents

attached_sources

The conversation-scoped working set — pinned sandbox files / uploads / web refs that persist across turns and never enter a corpus, never ground, never cite (ADR-0022 refined).

conversation_id · kind · ref · pinned_by · removed_at
conversationsparticipantsinterval

runs

One agent execution. Producer-private; work-item-bound or ad-hoc; the defensibility record's root.

conversation_id · requested_by · state · model
conversationsparticipantsappend-only

steps

The run's audited tree — retrieve / draft / ground-check / cite leaves with model, tokens, source set, rail outcomes and the ADR-0037 egress facts.

run_id · kind · source_set · rail_outcomes · egress_*
runsappend-only
DRAWER 4

Output & signal

drawer4-output.ts

What a run proposes and what the human did with it. Signals are the moat's raw stream — partitioned by organisation, never pooled across the wall (ADR-0026).

suggestions

A proposed edit into a document — grounded-only by rule; hidden presentationally once one is accepted, rows retained.

run_id · work_item_id · sandbox_document_id · content · resolution
runswork_itemssandbox_documents

citations

The grounded source behind each claim — version identity + claim span; rendered as the source chip (T-105).

suggestion_id · step_id · version_id · claim_span
suggestionsstepsversions

signals

Accept / edit / reject captured per suggestion — the behavioural stream that steers, never trains or grounds (ADR-0002/0026).

suggestion_id · action · by
suggestionsparticipantsappend-only
